title: Alsace
subtitle: German grapes, French style
objectives: Explain its grand cru and sweet wine rules

steps.title: Rain shadow
steps.body: Alsace lies between the Vosges mountains and the Rhine, on France's border with Germany. The Vosges block rain from the west, so Colmar is one of France's driest cities. Long, sunny, dry autumns let grapes ripen fully. The region switched between France and Germany several times, which shaped its grapes and bottles.
steps.highlight: Vosges rain shadow, dry and sunny

steps.title: Grapes on the label
steps.body: Unlike most of France, Alsace labels name the grape. The four noble grapes are Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat. Most wines are single-variety and unoaked, or aged in old foudres. Pinot Noir is the only red. Alsace is one of the few French regions that uses a tall, slim bottle called a flûte, by law.
steps.highlight: Grapes on the label, tall bottles

steps.prompt: Unlike most French regions, Alsace labels usually name the ____.
steps.explanation: Alsace names the variety, a habit shared with Germany.

steps.title: Grand crus and late harvests
steps.body: Alsace has 51 Grand Cru vineyards, mostly limited to the four noble grapes. Late harvest wines are labelled Vendanges Tardives; wines from noble rot berries are Sélection de Grains Nobles, with higher minimum sugar. Crémant d'Alsace is France's most produced crémant.

steps.prompt: Which are noble grapes of Alsace?
steps.explanation: The four noble grapes are Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat. Chardonnay is grown in Alsace, mainly for Crémant, but isn't one of them, and Sauvignon Blanc plays almost no role.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Alsace is dry and sunny in the rain shadow of the Vosges
Labels name the grape; Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat are noble
51 Grand Crus, plus VT and SGN for late harvest and noble rot
